newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PacDun to keep 1997 div at 96 levels.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PacDun to keep 1997 div at 96 levels.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific Dunlop Ltd said it plans to pay the same dividend in the 1996/97 year to June 30 as it did in 1995/96.
This is expected to result in a more conservative payout ratio, the company said.
Pacific Dunlop paid a total dividend of 14 cents a share in the 1995/96 year, down from 22.5 cents in 1994/95.

"The present intention of directors is for the 1997 dividend to remain a the 1996 level as we drive for improved performance, and this is expected to result in a more conservative pay-out ratio," Pacific Dunlop chairman John Gough said in a statement.
"Directors also proposes adjusting the 1997 year interim dividend to achieve a balanced payout between the interim and final dividends in the full year," Gough said.

"We regret the immediate effect the dividend decision will have on shareholders. The decision does, however, help Pacific Dunlop maintain a strong balance sheet and the capacity for investment and growth as appropriate opportunities arise."
Pacific Dunlop paid a final dividend of three cents in the six months to June 30, 1996 on top of the 11 cents paid in the first half of 1995/96.

Pacific Dunlop earlier reported a net loss of A$132.74 million for the year to June 30, 1996, compared with a net profit of A$94.2 million a year earlier. The 1995/96 result was hit by an abnormal loss of A$284.55 million.
At 3.05 p.m. (0505 GMT), Pacific Dunlop shares were seven cents up at A$2.73.
